title: Introducing Meta Quest 3 | Coming This Fall

hook.text: Introducing Meta Quest 3 / Reimagined and redesigned / From the inside out
hook.technique_other: cinematic product reveal: brand mark zoom-through into a hero 3D render with an exploded view

cta.text: Meta Quest 3 From $499 / Coming this fall

summary.tone: Energetic, aspirational consumer-hardware launch: polished pastel and dark-gradient 3D product renders alternate with warm lifestyle and gameplay footage, driven by music and short kinetic captions rather than narration.

signature_moments.description: The Meta mark zooms through into a macro product render, pulls back to the hero headset with controllers, and ends in an exploded view with 'From the inside out' set in the gap between the layers.
signature_moments.why_premium: One continuous camera move links brand, product and engineering story, and putting text inside the exploded geometry reads as designed for the product rather than overlaid.

signature_moments.description: The camera pushes into the headset's centre sensor pill, which becomes a glowing tunnel that 'Breakthrough' flies out of before it smears into 'Meta Reality'.
signature_moments.why_premium: Using a real product detail as the transition portal (a match-cut style zoom-through) makes the cut feel motivated and gives the feature reveal energy.

signature_moments.description: 'With natural depth perception' is placed word by word in 3D space inside a mixed-reality tabletop battle, camera-tracked and occluded by the figurines.
signature_moments.why_premium: The typography itself shows the feature (depth); 3D tracking and roto occlusion are expensive craft that flat captions cannot match.

hook.evidence: The cold open goes straight from the brand mark into a striking product reveal and exploded view within about 8 s. It is visually strong but a classic launch reveal rather than a tension or problem hook.

clarity.evidence: Each shot carries one short benefit caption (40% slimmer, double the GPU power, full-color passthrough, TruTouch haptics, 500+ titles), backed by a matching visual, and it closes on product, price and launch window.

ui_showcase.evidence: This is a hardware launch, so there is no software UI. The showcase is product renders plus gameplay and mixed-reality footage, which is competent but shows no interface flows; the game-tile wall is the nearest thing to UI.

motion_polish.evidence: Caption motion is consistent throughout (blur-in, word-by-word builds, horizontal smear exits), with motivated zoom-throughs (logo, sensor pill, lens) and 3D-tracked occluded type. The closing kinetic line is cut on the music.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchors only (not heard): a 126 BPM music bed at -16.5 LUFS integrated, with 73 SFX candidates that are mostly 'unsure' or 'swoosh_reverse' and cluster on transitions and caption smears (e.g. 1.8-8.4 s, 47.9-52.6 s, 65-71 s). This suggests a music-led mix with whoosh accents, but quality cannot be confirmed beyond that.

vo_script_quality.evidence: There is no voice-over. The transcript is 12 fragmentary words (w0-w11), probably song lyrics or ambient vocal, and all of the copy is on-screen text.

brand_consistency.evidence: One sans family and centred caption system throughout, recurring pastel and dark purple-teal gradient backdrops, the Meta mark at the open and in the end lockup, and a consistent product render style.

works_muted.evidence: Every claim is carried by on-screen captions and visuals, and there is no narration, so the story, price and launch window are fully readable with the sound off.

overall.evidence: A tightly paced 77 s launch film that combines high-end 3D product renders, lifestyle and gameplay footage, and a disciplined kinetic caption system. Each feature gets one clear beat, and it ends on a crisp price-and-date end card.

localization_friendliness.notes: Not dependent on VO, but all copy is baked into the picture as animated captions, some of it 3D-tracked and occluded inside the footage (s019), plus price and age footnotes. Localising means re-rendering the type layers, and the per-word kinetic builds would need re-timing for longer languages.

annotation.focal_element: Meta infinity mark, very low contrast against a near-black background
annotation.transition_other: video start (anchors give no transition into the first shot)
annotation.what_happens: A single held frame of the large Meta infinity mark, dim grey on black, fading up from darkness as a cold open.
annotation.build_rebuild: Render the brand mark SVG centred at about 60% frame width on a near-black background at roughly 15% opacity and fade its opacity up over the shot's 0.46 s.

annotation.focal_element: Rendered Meta Quest 3 headset front with floating controllers, then the headset in three-quarter view with the headline over it
annotation.typography: Clean geometric/humanist sans, dark ink on pale gradient. 'Introducing' small medium weight above a larger semibold 'Meta Quest 3' lockup, sentence case, normal tracking; later 'Reimagined and redesigned' semibold sentence case centred over the product. Possibly Meta's brand sans (Optimistic) - low confidence.
annotation.what_happens: The Meta mark brightens and lightens to grey, then the camera zooms through into a tight close-up of the headset front sensors on a pastel pink-to-blue gradient; it pulls back to reveal the headset floating centre with two controllers flanking it while 'Introducing / Meta Quest 3' resolves from a motion-blurred smear. Around 4.0 s everything smears left with directional motion blur and the headset reappears rotated three-quarter with 'Reimagined' then 'and redesigned' appended word-by-word; the shot ends as the faceplate lifts off into an exploded view of the internals.
annotation.build_rebuild: Scale the logo up past camera into a 3D product render close-up, pull back to a centred headset with controllers left and right, blur-in a two-line title (small kicker over bold product name), then exit with a horizontal motion-blur push and append 'Reimagined' + 'and redesigned' word-by-word over a rotated product view before animating the faceplate upward on the Y axis.

annotation.focal_element: Exploded view of the headset: faceplate, camera bracket and internal boards separated vertically, with the headline sitting in the gap
annotation.typography: Large semibold sans, sentence case, dark ink, normal tracking, centred and inserted between the exploded layers so components sit above and below it.
annotation.what_happens: The exploded headset holds with a slow drift as the top layers continue to separate slightly; 'From the inside out' sits in the gap between the floating faceplate parts and the open chassis.
annotation.build_rebuild: Stack separated product layers (faceplate, bracket, board, chassis) with a slow eased Y-separation and place a centred semibold headline in the vertical gap between the upper and lower layers.

annotation.focal_element: Two headsets side by side from below/behind (Quest 2 left, Quest 3 right) with the '40% slimmer' stat centred between them
annotation.transition_other: motion-blurred entry: the stat '40' arrives smeared and a blurred element sweeps in from the left (whip-like, not classified by code)
on_screen_text: As compared to Quest 2 excluding the facial interfaces.
annotation.typography: Stat '40% slimmer' in large semibold sans, lowercase word after the numeral, dark ink; footnote disclaimer in small light/regular grey sans centred near the bottom edge.
annotation.what_happens: A side-by-side comparison of the old and new headset; the number '40' blurs in and resolves to '40% slimmer' with a footnote disclaimer. Around 10.5 s the facial interfaces drop in from below with motion blur, the text clears, and at the end both headsets rotate quickly with heavy motion blur into the next angle.
annotation.build_rebuild: Place two product renders in left/right halves, blur-in a centred stat label between them with a small footnote at the bottom, then slide the facial-interface parts up from below the frame and exit by rotating both renders with a motion-blur whip.

annotation.focal_element: Quest 2 (left) and Quest 3 (right) in side profile with straps, facing each other to show the depth difference
annotation.transition_other: continuation of the motion-blurred rotation that ends s004 (code classified as other)
annotation.what_happens: Both headsets hang in profile on the pastel gradient, angled toward each other, with a very slow drift so the slimmer front profile of the new model is visible; no text.
annotation.build_rebuild: Show two product renders in profile, left one angled down-right and right one angled up-left, on the same pastel gradient, with a slow 1-2% drift for the 1.3 s hold.

annotation.focal_element: Inside of the headset facial interface: two lens openings framed by knit fabric padding, symmetric around a small center sensor
annotation.what_happens: A symmetric, dark product render looks into the headset through its lenses toward a soft pastel sky; the camera slowly pushes in so the fabric texture of the padding becomes readable over the roughly one-second shot.
annotation.build_rebuild: Render the headset interior head-on in a 3D scene with a pastel gradient backdrop behind the lenses and animate a 1 s camera dolly-in of about 10 percent scale with an ease-out curve.

annotation.focal_element: Macro detail of the dark knit fabric on the headset padding curving across the frame against a pastel gradient
annotation.what_happens: A macro render sweeps along the curved knit padding with shallow depth of field; by the second sampled frame (0:14.5) the picture already shows the white woven head strap arching against the same pastel sky, so the shot appears to contain a quick material-detail sequence.
annotation.build_rebuild: Show a macro 3D close-up of a textured fabric surface diagonal across the frame with a shallow depth-of-field blur and a slow lateral camera drift of about 0.6 s, on a pink-to-blue gradient background.

annotation.focal_element: A woman wearing the white headset dancing/playing in a warm-lit living room, with a large glowing white letter overlaid on her torso
annotation.typography: Single oversized white sans-serif capital letter with a soft glow/motion blur; it is the first visible glyph of the kinetic word PLAY that completes in s009.
annotation.what_happens: The keyframe still shows the white head strap render, while the 0:15.0 contact-sheet frame shows lifestyle footage of a player lunging in a living room as a glowing letter flies in; the cut from product render to lifestyle footage happens inside this short shot.
annotation.build_rebuild: Hard cut from the strap render to handheld lifestyle footage and fly a single large white capital letter in with a scale-down plus motion blur over 0.3 s, centered on the subject.

annotation.focal_element: The player in the headset in a living room, with the scattered letters PLAY resolving into the caption 'Play in maximum comfort'
annotation.typography: First, oversized white uppercase sans-serif letters P-L-A-Y scattered at different sizes and offsets; then a centered single-line caption in a bold geometric sans-serif, sentence case, normal tracking, white with no box. Font guess (low confidence): Meta's Optimistic Display.
annotation.what_happens: Big kinetic letters spelling PLAY float over the dancing player, blur away and are replaced by the centered caption 'Play in maximum comfort', which blurs in word by word (the keyframe shows 'in maximum comfort' still semi-transparent). The shot ends on black, with the next caption 'game-changing performance' already arriving as a horizontal streak.
annotation.build_rebuild: Over full-bleed footage, animate four oversized uppercase letters in with staggered scale and offset, blur them out, then blur-in a centered white bold sans caption word by word with 80 ms stagger and hold it for about 1 s before cutting to black.

annotation.focal_element: A gold Snapdragon-branded chip on a dark circuit board that lights up with blue and orange traces
on_screen_text: Graphics performance of next-gen Snapdragon chip vs. Meta Quest 2 chip.
annotation.typography: Main captions are centered white bold geometric sans-serif in sentence case with normal tracking; the transition between captions uses a horizontal motion-streak blur. 'Snapdragon' is the brand wordmark printed on the chip. The disclaimer is a small light-weight sans-serif footnote centered at the bottom.
annotation.what_happens: 'Enjoy game-changing performance' sits over a dark, blurred circuit environment; the caption smears away horizontally as a tilted gold Snapdragon chip swings into view. The camera settles on the chip while the board's traces light up in blue and orange, the caption 'Double the GPU processing power' appears in front of it, and a footnote explains the comparison basis.
annotation.build_rebuild: Hold a centered caption over a dark defocused 3D board, wipe it out with a horizontal motion-blur streak while a tilted chip model rotates to near-flat with an ease-out, then light circuit traces outward with an emissive glow and fade in the second caption plus a small bottom footnote.

annotation.focal_element: First-person VR gameplay in a desert canyon (player hands holding a whip and a glowing blade, enemies ahead) under the centered caption

annotation.what_happens: In-game footage plays as the caption 'Faster and smoother experiences' assembles letter by letter with a blur and vertical offset, then holds while the player swings a blade; by 0:24.0 the frame has returned to the headset lens render with the caption 'Higher Resolution Displays'.
annotation.build_rebuild: Play full-bleed gameplay capture and reveal a centered white caption per character with a 20 px rise, blur-to-sharp and 25 ms stagger, holding it for about 1.5 s before a hard cut to the next product render.

annotation.focal_element: Feature headline centred between the two lens openings of the headset interior
annotation.typography: Clean geometric sans, semibold, title case, normal tracking, white, single centred line (low-confidence guess: Meta's Optimistic Display-like face)
annotation.what_happens: A symmetric render of the headset's inside, looking out through the two lenses at a soft pastel sky, holds while the feature label sits centred; by the last sampled frame the view has already changed to the game character with the next caption mid-reveal.
annotation.build_rebuild: Place a dark headset-interior render full-bleed, overlay a centred white semibold title-case label, and hold it for about 1 s before cutting to the in-headset content.

annotation.focal_element: A CG armoured game character with a sword on his shoulder, caption across his chest
annotation.typography: Same sans as the feature labels, semibold, sentence case, normal tracking, white over the scene; words reveal separately ("Clearer" and "sharper" visible first, spread apart, then the line closes up)

annotation.focal_element: Centred kinetic headline on a soft pastel gradient

annotation.focal_element: Front of the white Quest 3 headset with its three vertical sensor pills and logo
annotation.what_happens: A brief (0.42 s) frontal hero render of the headset fills the frame against a light gradient.

annotation.focal_element: Words emerging from a blue tunnel formed by the headset's centre sensor pill

annotation.focal_element: A young man on a green sofa handling the headset in a sunlit living room
annotation.what_happens: Warm live-action lifestyle shot: the man sits on the sofa holding the headset, with a table blurred in the foreground and window light flaring behind; only one frame is sampled so any motion is not visible.

annotation.focal_element: The headset held in first-person POV over a coffee table, then the view through its lenses revealing a miniature fantasy castle on the table

annotation.focal_element: Kinetic caption 'With natural depth perception' tracked into a living-room battle scene of fantasy figurines and a glowing die, with the user in the headset behind

annotation.typography: Bold geometric sans-serif, lower/sentence case; words are placed in 3D space at different sizes and depths ('depth' largest), tracked to the scene and partially occluded by characters
annotation.what_happens: The previous caption holds briefly, then the camera dives into the figurine battle; 'With natural depth perception' arrives as words scattered in 3D space that move with the camera and get occluded by figurines, before a spell effect clears the text and the shot ends on a wide of the user seated in the headset.

on_screen_text: Transform your home into a virtual

annotation.focal_element: CG renders of the new Touch controllers: macro thumbstick close-up, then a pair of controllers floating on a soft gradient

annotation.build_rebuild: Hold a centred sans caption over the hand plate and, near the end, apply a few-frame position jitter plus an accent colour shift to the last word to simulate a haptic buzz.

annotation.shot_type_other: product render of the headset lens that zooms through into a fast montage of VR gameplay footage with one-word captions
annotation.focal_element: The headset lens (text appears inside it), then single centred caption words over each game clip
annotation.typography: Clean geometric sans-serif, bold/semibold, sentence case, normal tracking, white; 'Jump into' sits inside the lens in a smaller italic-looking weight; a third word after 'Jump into' is motion-blurred and unreadable. Font guess (low confidence): Meta's in-house sans.

annotation.build_rebuild: Scale a lens render up past the viewport with a radial-blur zoom-through into a video, then cut clips every ~1 s on the beat, each with one centred bold white word that fades in with a slight blur.

annotation.focal_element: An ornate puzzle box on a table manipulated by translucent tracked hands, with a centred two-line caption
annotation.typography: Same bold geometric sans-serif, sentence case, white, centred two lines; words reveal sequentially (first 'Immersive games', then 'and', then 'experiences' fading in).
annotation.what_happens: First-person VR footage of hand-tracking hands turning a carved puzzle box on a cluttered table while the caption builds word by word in the centre.

annotation.focal_element: Avatar golf scenes with the caption building in the centre
annotation.typography: Bold geometric sans-serif, sentence case, white, single line; words fade in left to right ('Plus all' solid while 'your' is still faint).
annotation.what_happens: A canyon mini-golf clip with a cartoon avatar swinging, then (an undetected cut within this shot) a night-time avatar golf range with a fiery ball trail; the caption 'Plus all your old favorites' builds word by word and persists across the cut.

annotation.shot_type_other: kinetic-type gradient card intercut with a short lifestyle footage insert, ending on the next type card

annotation.typography: Bold geometric sans-serif, sentence case, white, normal tracking, single centred line; 'Powerful' arrives larger and motion-blurred. Same family as all earlier captions (low-confidence guess: Meta's Optimistic Display).

annotation.what_happens: Low-angle live-action shot of a player dancing/lunging in a mid-century living room, with backlit curtains and a sun flare behind her; the camera drifts slightly as she moves. No text.

annotation.focal_element: Caption 'Meta Quest yet' on the dark gradient, then a woman putting the headset on
annotation.typography: Bold geometric sans-serif, title-case product name plus lowercase 'yet', white, normal tracking, single centred line; 'yet' blurs in last.

annotation.shot_type_other: lifestyle footage into a product-render push through the lenses, a product hero lockup with logo and price, then a title end card
annotation.focal_element: Headset and two controllers floating on the dark gradient above the 'Meta Quest 3 / From $499' lockup, then the end line 'Coming this fall'
annotation.typography: 'Meta Quest 3' is the brand wordmark lockup with the infinity mark, regular/medium weight, title case; 'From $499' bold sans directly below (it builds in, 'From' first); the age note is a small light sans footnote near the bottom; 'Coming this fall' is a bold sentence-case white line centred on the gradient, entering with a heavy horizontal motion-blur smear.

pattern.description: One title word on a soft gradient is replaced by the next: the outgoing word streaks sideways with heavy horizontal motion blur, a 1-2 frame bright blurred flash covers the swap, and the incoming two-word title appears small and scales up to its settled size.
pattern.why_premium: The swap is hidden inside a very short smear-plus-flash, so the beat feels like an energetic whip without a cut; the incoming title growing into place gives a sense of arrival and keeps the eye centered.

build_hint.remotion: Old word: interpolate(frame,[0,3],[0,200]) for translateX with blur 0->24px and opacity 1->0 (Easing.in(Easing.cubic)); flash overlay opacity [2,3,4]->[0,0.8,0]; new word scale via spring({frame:frame-4,fps,config:{damping:200,stiffness:220,mass:1}}) mapped 0.55->1 with opacity interpolate [4,6]->[0,1].

events.notes: Outgoing 'Breakthrough' is not on the end frame, so it is described inside the b01 element rather than listed separately. camera.move reports pan_right with scale 2.05; this is driven by the text smear and the flash frame, not a real camera move on a static gradient. No SFX candidates and no nearby words.

elements.label: Title word swap: 'Breakthrough' smears out horizontally, 'Meta Reality' appears small and scales up
Gradient background washes to a bright blurred flash for ~1-2 frames, then returns

pattern.description: The device is brought toward camera until its lens openings fill the frame; a two-lens (binocular) mask then grows outward, revealing the in-headset view, and the mask edges dissolve into a full-frame POV with a centered feature caption.
pattern.why_premium: It puts the viewer inside the product with no cut: the hardware itself becomes the transition, so the feature (passthrough) is shown from the user's point of view at the moment it is named on screen.

build_hint.remotion: Headset layer scale interpolate(frame,[0,9],[1,2.2],{easing:Easing.in(Easing.quad)}); POV layer inside an SVG two-ellipse mask whose scale is spring({frame:frame-8,fps,config:{damping:200,stiffness:160,mass:1}}) mapped 0.6->3 so the mask exits the frame; caption opacity interpolate [12,16]->[0,1].

events.notes: Live-action/composited footage, not UI. The headset push-toward-camera is in the footage itself (camera.move is none). No taxonomy pattern covers a hardware-lens zoom-through, hence 'other'. The caption is already visible at f915; its exact fade timing is unclear from the filmstrip. No SFX candidates.

elements.label: Footage: headset lifted to the viewer until its lenses fill frame; the binocular lens view then expands to full-frame passthrough POV
Feature caption appearing over the passthrough view

pattern.description: A CG product render camera orbits and pulls back from a macro detail (thumbstick) to a hero view of both controllers, while the feature caption is swapped: the old line streaks off with horizontal motion blur and the next feature line fades in once the new angle settles.
pattern.why_premium: The continuous CG orbit replaces a cut, so the product never leaves the screen; the caption change rides the fastest part of the move, hiding the swap, and the new line lands on a calm, centered hero composition.

build_hint.remotion: Drive the 3D camera (e.g. @remotion/three) with interpolate(frame,[0,18],[0,1],{easing:Easing.inOut(Easing.cubic)}) for orbit angle and dolly; old caption translateX/blur/opacity interpolate [3,6] with Easing.in(Easing.cubic); new caption opacity via spring({frame:frame-14,fps,config:{damping:200,stiffness:150,mass:1}}).

events.notes: Outgoing caption is not on the end frame, so it is described within b02. camera.move is none (pan_x is content motion of the CG render, not a filming camera move). Pattern could alternatively be kinetic_word_reveal (the caption swap) but the dominant motion is the product orbit. SFX: the stem shows a regular percussion pulse, so per-candidate SFX vs music is uncertain.

elements.label: CG controller render: close-up on the thumbstick orbits/pulls back to reveal both controllers floating
Caption swap: 'Meet our redesigned controllers' smears out horizontally, 'With TruTouch' fades in

pattern.description: Over live footage, a one-line caption assembles word by word: each word slides in from the right with a horizontal motion-blur smear and settles, and the last word ('feel') lands with a playful per-letter vertical offset that echoes its meaning.
pattern.why_premium: Fast blurred slides give the type physical momentum to match the hand movement in the footage, and the per-letter wobble on the key word adds a tactile accent exactly on the feature being sold (haptic feel).

build_hint.gsap: Split caption into words (and the last word into chars). tl.from(words,{x:80,autoAlpha:0,filter:'blur(12px)',duration:0.2,ease:'power3.out',stagger:0.05}).from(lastWordChars,{y:()=>gsap.utils.random(-10,10),duration:0.35,ease:'back.out(2)',stagger:0.03},'>-0.1')
build_hint.remotion: Per word i: progress = spring({frame:frame-2*i,fps,config:{damping:200,stiffness:300,mass:0.6}}); translateX = interpolate(progress,[0,1],[80,0]); blur = interpolate(progress,[0,1],[12,0]); opacity = progress. For chars of the last word use spring with damping:10 (slight overshoot) on translateY from a per-char offset.

events.notes: Small diff boxes b03-b08 are incidental footage motion (fabric/background), not designed elements, so not listed. The letters of 'feel' in the end frame are still at uneven heights; whether this is a settled stylistic offset or still mid-animation is unclear. SFX x041 vs music beat is ambiguous.

elements.label: Caption builds word by word: each word streaks in from the right with motion blur; the final word 'feel' arrives with letters bobbing at slightly different heights
Live-action footage of hands holding the controllers; a bright horizontal light streak washes over the frame at the start of the burst

pattern.description: The shot pushes into the headset lens; a radial (zoom) blur streaks the frame, the next scene emerges scaled-down from the blur, and the overlay word swaps from 'Jump into new' to 'Deeper' through the same blur so the text change rides the transition.
pattern.why_premium: The lens acts as a literal portal, so the cut carries meaning (entering the world); the radial blur hides the seam in about a third of a second, and swapping the kinetic word inside the blur keeps the type beat continuous instead of cutting it separately.

build_hint.gsap: Outgoing layer: gsap.to(sceneA, {scale: 1.8, filter: 'blur(14px)', duration: 0.18, ease: 'power2.in'}) with a radial-blur overlay opacity 0->1. Incoming layer: gsap.fromTo(sceneB, {scale: 1.25, filter: 'blur(14px)', opacity: 0}, {scale: 1, filter: 'blur(0px)', opacity: 1, duration: 0.25, ease: 'power3.out'}, '<0.1'); word swap: fromTo(word, {scale: 1.6, filter: 'blur(10px)', opacity: 0}, {scale: 1, filter: 'blur(0px)', opacity: 1, duration: 0.3, ease: 'power3.out'}, '<').
build_hint.remotion: Two Sequences overlapping ~3 frames; sceneA scale = interpolate(frame, [0, 6], [1, 1.8], {easing: Easing.in(Easing.quad)}) with blur; sceneB and the word use spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 180}}) mapped to scale 1.25->1 (word 1.6->1) and blur 14->0px; radial-blur overlay opacity peaks at the overlap.

events.notes: camera.move is 'none' per facts though the whole frame visibly zooms; reported as content scale on b01, not a camera move. Outgoing text 'Jump into new' is not on the end frame, so it has no box; its blur-out is folded into the b02 swap description.

elements.label: Full-frame scene: headset lens close-up zooms through into red game world
Overlay word 'Deeper' replacing 'Jump into new'

pattern.description: A single centred overlay word sits on top of fast-cut gameplay; on the cut to new footage the word swaps ('Deeper' to 'Larger'), with the swap masked by a white smoke burst in the footage, continuing a one-word-per-shot comparative sequence.
pattern.why_premium: One bold word per beat keeps the copy at a glance-read pace while the footage carries the proof; the word holds its centre position across cuts so the eye never has to search, and the swap is hidden inside visual action, not a separate text animation.

build_hint.gsap: Timeline per beat: tl.set(clipA, {autoAlpha: 0}).set(clipB, {autoAlpha: 1}) on the cut (hard cut, no ease); then tl.to(wordOld, {autoAlpha: 0, duration: 0.08, ease: 'none'}).fromTo(wordNew, {autoAlpha: 0}, {autoAlpha: 1, duration: 0.1, ease: 'power1.out'}, '<0.04'); keep both words absolutely centred in the same slot.
build_hint.remotion: Sequence per clip with hard cuts (no transition); word layer as its own Sequence offset ~4 frames after the cut, opacity = interpolate(frame, [0, 3], [0, 1], {extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}); no spring, the swap is near-instant.

events.notes: The word swap lags the footage cut by about 3 frames ('Deeper' still visible on f1322 and f1325 over the new scene) and coincides with the smoke burst; whether the text fades or hard-swaps is not clear at this frame spacing. b03 (trap display '00') only moves with the hand-held prop inside the footage, so it is folded into b01, not listed.

elements.label: Full-frame footage: hard cut from red game world to Ghostbusters VR firehouse scene, with a white smoke burst across the frame
elements.change_other: hard cut to new gameplay footage, followed by an in-footage smoke burst

elements.label: Overlay word swaps 'Deeper' to 'Larger'

pattern.description: Centred one-word overlay over fast gameplay cuts: the footage cuts, a horizontal white light-streak flash crosses the frame, and the word swaps from 'Larger' to 'Richer' through a short horizontal smear, holding the same centred slot.
pattern.why_premium: The light-streak flash and the text smear share one direction, so cut and copy change read as a single gesture; the fixed word slot and one-word cadence keep the comparison series ('Deeper', 'Larger', 'Richer') rhythmic and instantly legible over busy footage.

build_hint.gsap: On each beat: hard-cut clips (tl.set autoAlpha); tl.fromTo(streakOverlay, {xPercent: -60, autoAlpha: 0}, {xPercent: 60, autoAlpha: 1, duration: 0.2, ease: 'power2.inOut', yoyo: true, repeat: 1}); word swap in the same slot: tl.to(wordOld, {filter: 'blur(8px)', scaleX: 1.3, autoAlpha: 0, duration: 0.1, ease: 'power2.in'}, '<').fromTo(wordNew, {filter: 'blur(8px)', scaleX: 1.3, autoAlpha: 0}, {filter: 'blur(0px)', scaleX: 1, autoAlpha: 1, duration: 0.15, ease: 'power3.out'}, '>-0.03').
build_hint.remotion: Hard-cut Sequences; a streak overlay layer with opacity interpolate(frame, [0, 3, 6], [0, 1, 0]); word layer: out over 3 frames (blur 0->8px, scaleX 1->1.3), new word in with spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 220}}) driving blur 8->0 and scaleX 1.3->1.

events.notes: Cannot tell from the stills whether the white streaks are a designed overlay or part of the game footage; same visual device appears at e007. The large energy dip between f1339 and f1344 suggests the cut itself is near f1340 and the streak/word swap follows about 4-6 frames later.

elements.label: Full-frame footage: cut from Ghostbusters firehouse to amber cave climbing scene, crossed by horizontal white light streaks
elements.change_other: hard cut to new gameplay footage plus a horizontal white light-streak flash over the cut

elements.label: Overlay word swaps 'Larger' to 'Richer' through a horizontal motion smear

pattern.description: A radial zoom blur pulls the frame out of the snowy footage and resolves on a curved wall of game-footage tiles; the headline 'From our library of ... titles' flies in with the same blur and scale, landing centred over the wall while the number slot rolls in.
pattern.why_premium: Text and backdrop share one blur-and-scale move, so the headline feels embedded in the space rather than pasted on; the curved tile wall instantly communicates catalogue breadth, and the zoom hides the cut in about a third of a second.

build_hint.gsap: tl.to(clipA, {scale: 1.6, filter: 'blur(16px)', duration: 0.15, ease: 'power2.in'}) then tl.fromTo(tileWall, {scale: 1.35, filter: 'blur(16px)'}, {scale: 1, filter: 'blur(0px)', duration: 0.33, ease: 'power3.out'}, '<0.08'); headline parts fromTo({scale: 1.5, filter: 'blur(10px)', autoAlpha: 0}, {scale: 1, filter: 'blur(0px)', autoAlpha: 1, duration: 0.25, ease: 'power3.out', stagger: 0.03}, '<'); number slot: roll digits with a yPercent tween per digit (stagger 0.03).
build_hint.remotion: Overlapping Sequences (~3 frames); tile wall and headline driven by one spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 170}}) mapped to scale 1.35->1 (text 1.5->1) and blur 16->0px; outgoing clip scale interpolate(frame, [0, 4], [1, 1.6], {easing: Easing.in(Easing.quad)}); digits as translateY columns per character.

events.notes: camera.move is pull_out (scale 0.77), consistent with the wall resolving smaller. The number between 'of' and 'titles' remains blurred and illegible in the settled frame (possibly deliberately obscured or still rolling), so it is a manual box with is_text false and no text. b04 and b05 are in-tile game text that only move with the wall, so they are folded into b01. Same transition device as e006.

elements.label: Curved wall of game-footage tiles revealed out of a radial zoom blur from the snowy mountain shot
Headline lead-in 'From our library of'
Number slot in the headline (illegible digits roll in, then stay blurred)
Headline end word 'titles'

pattern.description: Hard cut from lifestyle footage into an extreme close-up of the headset's lenses; the product then rotates and pulls back in one continuous move while the two controllers sweep in from the frame edges and settle symmetrically below it, ending on a clean hero lockup on a dark gradient.
pattern.why_premium: Starting inside the product (the lenses) and orbiting out to the full silhouette turns a static packshot into a reveal; the controllers converging from the edges create a balanced triangular lockup, and motion blur plus a decelerating settle make the 3D render feel physical.

build_hint.gsap: Hard cut (tl.set) to the hero layer; tl.fromTo(headset, {scale: 3, rotationY: -70, filter: 'blur(8px)'}, {scale: 1, rotationY: 0, filter: 'blur(0px)', duration: 0.45, ease: 'power3.out'}); tl.fromTo([ctrlL, ctrlR], {x: (i) => i ? 400 : -400, rotation: (i) => i ? 25 : -25, scale: 1.6}, {x: 0, rotation: 0, scale: 1, duration: 0.35, ease: 'power3.out', stagger: 0}, '<0.1').
build_hint.remotion: Headset: const s = spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 120}}); scale interpolate(s, [0, 1], [3, 1]), rotateY interpolate(s, [0, 1], [-70, 0]) deg, blur 8->0px. Controllers start 3 frames later with spring damping 200 stiffness 160, translateX +/-400 -> 0 and rotate +/-25 -> 0 deg. No overshoot.

events.notes: camera.move is pan_right; visually it reads as a 3D product orbit/pull-back in a render, so motion is assigned to the product layers rather than a separate camera element. Controller manual boxes are estimated on the end frame. Both SFX left unsure.

elements.label: Hero shot: cut from lifestyle footage to a macro of the headset lenses, which spins and pulls back to the front-facing Quest 3 headset on a dark blue gradient
Left Touch controller slides in from the left edge and rotates to rest
Right Touch controller slides in from the right edge and rotates to rest
